Shade uses this accessibility service to draw overlay content at full opacity. On Android 12 and above, regular overlays are limited to 80% opacity, which may not fully obscure detected content. Enabling this service allows Shade to display the overlay at any opacity level you choose.\n\nScreen content is captured for on-device processing only. No data is sent anywhere — Shade does not have internet permission.
Shade needs a few permissions to work

Required so Shade can place a fully opaque cover over detected content and detect app switches for auto-start. Without this service, Android may limit overlays and auto-starting feature won\'t work.\nPrivacy: processing stays on-device only. Shade has no internet permission.

Shade needs Accessibility Service to:
• place a reliable full-opacity cover over detected content
• detect when selected apps open (auto-start)

How to enable:
1. Tap "Request permission".
2. In Accessibility settings, open "Installed apps" or "Installed services".
3. Select Shade and turn it ON.
Required to keep Shade running in the background. You\'ll also see controls to quickly stop or clear the cover.
Single app recording is not supported on this device. Using experimental full screen mode.
Single app recording is not supported on this device. Shade will use the experimental full screen mode instead. This mode might not provide the best experience and quality.
Start Shade automatically when selected apps are opened
Control how much content is blurred. Large pixels completely hide details, while small ones retain some features.
Something went wrong while starting detection.
Choose how Shade should detect and hide content
Set how strict detection should be. Lower values detect more but can mistakenly trigger on normal content. Higher values reduce false alerts but may miss some content.
Control how visible the cover is. Higher opacity hides content more completely, while lower opacity keeps more of the screen visible.

Select the size of the pixels used to hide content. Large pixels hide details and blur the image, small pixels retain some general features and colors.\nLarge pixels are easier to process and consume less resources.
Normal mode uses full rectangular boxes, which might hide nearby elements. Detailed mode recognizes the exact shape of people and only covers them.\nDetailed mode requires more processing power.

For the best detection quality, choose \"Single app\" in the next capture picker.\n\nIf you really need \"Entire screen\", enable \"Full Screen Mode\" in Advanced settings before starting. Even then, the experience and quality may still be less optimal than \"Single app\".
The first load for each model type can take a few minutes.\nStarting detection is usually much faster next times
Android blocks capture on banking apps, DRM videos, and FLAG_SECURE windows. Detection is paused on those surfaces.

Timer = a small waiting period after the blocker catches something.

For example:
If the timer is 10 minutes, the app keeps protection active for 10 minutes before normal access is restored.

It is NOT a timer that decides whether something is porn.
The AI decides that.
The timer only controls what happens AFTER a detection.
Instantly returns to device Home screen upon detection to stop viewing immediately.
Verifies detection over multiple consecutive frames before triggering cooldown. Prevents false alarms on swimwear, fitness, and ordinary photos.

What Shade can and cannot inspect

WHAT IS PROTECTED:
• Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Opera, Brave
• YouTube, Twitter/X, Reddit, TikTok, Instagram
• Webviews and streaming applications
• Full-screen media where capture is permitted

ANDROID SYSTEM RESTRICTIONS:
• FLAG_SECURE: Banking apps and secure windows prohibit capture (returns pitch black frames).
• DRM Media: Protected video (Netflix, Disney+) returns black frames to protect copyright.
• MediaProjection: Android 14+ requires explicit user consent per session and displays a system privacy indicator.
• Background Capture: Android security requires a visible foreground notification while recording.
